title: The Coding Club
text:
There were nine of us at the first session and four of us by the third. Coding, it turned out, was far less exciting than the poster had suggested.
Our project was a game in which a small green square had to avoid falling rocks. It sounds simple. It was not. The square fell through the floor. The rocks appeared inside one another. Once, for reasons we never established, the entire screen turned purple and refused to change back.
We spent six weeks fixing things that broke other things. Mr Prakash refused to tell us the answers. He would only ask, again and again, the same irritating question: what did you expect to happen, and what happened instead?
The game worked in the ninth week. It lasted about forty seconds and had no sound.
I have never been prouder of anything in my life.
